title: fancy-sign: the completion record, its fsig_v1_ token, the Ed25519 seal and verify()

contract.summary: The completion record has a CLOSED key set (type, version, envelope_id, as_sent_sha256, as_sent_bytes, final_sha256, signers, chain_head, nonce, key_id; signers carry id, name, email, signed_at, method, otp_seq, consent_seq). Its canonical bytes are sign/chain's canonical JSON of those keys only. token = "fsig_v1_" + sha256(canonical). seal = base64 Ed25519 detached signature of the canonical bytes (deterministic, so pinned). key_id = the first 16 hex characters of sha256(raw public key). verify(final, record, events?) stops at the first failure: completion_invalid, token_mismatch, seal_invalid, final_hash_mismatch, prefix_mismatch, chain_broken, chain_head_mismatch. See SPEC.md.

functions.publicKey: publicKey(seed) -> base64 Ed25519 public key for a 32-byte hex seed
functions.canonical: canonical(record) -> string, the bytes the token hashes and the seal signs
functions.verify: verify({pdf_base64, completion, events?, public_keys}) -> {ok, reason, checks: {seal, token, final_hash, prefix, chain}}; a check not reached is null

contract.referenceNote: Goldens are particle-academy/fancy-sign's Completion, Ed25519 (ext-sodium) and Verifier, written by fancy-sign-php/tests/Conformance/Export.php. The seed is fixed test data, never a real key. The PDFs are short synthetic byte strings: verify() checks hashes and a byte prefix and never parses PDF syntax.

notes: tests/discrimination-sign.test.ts verifies these rows with node:crypto alone (Ed25519 via crypto.sign(null, ...)), which is the claim the plan makes for the Node port: standard library only.
